title: Knee MRI — report-derived soft labels (lexicon)
subtitle: Weak labels for 4,407 knee MRI studies, read from ten-language reports
description:
Training targets for the RSNA Knee Abnormality Detection competition, where
**only 58 of 4,407 training studies carry expert labels** and the rest carry a
free-text radiology report instead. No report text exists at test time, so the
labeler is a training-time device only: it manufactures targets and never ships
in the submission.

Produced by a hand-built multilingual lexicon (`src/report_labeler.py`) across
ten languages — English is only 39% of the corpus, so Spanish and Turkish are
first-class rather than afterthoughts.

**Measured quality: macro AUC 0.769 against the 58 expert-labelled studies.**
Per-finding AUC tracks the abstain rate almost monotonically, which is the most
useful thing to know about it: Synovitis abstains on 72% of reports and scores
0.580, while Effusion abstains on 9% and scores 0.721.

**Design choice worth borrowing:** five channels, not a probability. Silence and
denial are different states and collapsing them is the single most damaging
thing a weak labeler can do here. Training masks the loss on abstentions.

**Access:** private. It is keyed by competition StudyInstanceUIDs and is
competition-derived data, which may not be redistributed.

resources.description: One row per training study (4,407). Twelve soft target scores, one per finding, plus a five-way supervision channel per finding recording HOW each score was reached: asserted, hedged, low_severity, negated, or absent. `absent` means the labeler had nothing to say, and training masks the loss on those rather than teaching them as negatives — a report that never mentions the ACL is not a report saying the ACL is intact. Also carries the detected report language. No report text.

fields.name: lang
fields.description: Detected report language, ten in the corpus

fields.name: <finding>
fields.description: Soft score in [0,1], or null where the labeler abstained

resources.description: DICOM header scan over 24,386 series and 819,635 slices, headers only — no pixels were read. Carries pixel spacing, slice counts, laterality, anatomical plane and the scanner fields used to build the fold-grouping fingerprint. Grouping on that fingerprint matters: random K-fold inflates macro AUC by 0.087 on this dataset, because no site column exists anywhere and the scanner is the leak.
